title: Total Internal Reflection
page_title: Total Internal Reflection | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Physics Revision Notes 2018

blocks.md:
- Total internal reflection (TIR) occurs when: **The angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle and the incident refractive index***** n***<sub>***1***</sub>** is greater than the refractive index of the material at the boundary *****n***<sub>***2***</sub>
- Therefore, the **two** conditions for total internal reflection are:

  - The angle of incidence, *θ*<sub>*1*</sub> > the critical angle, *C*
  - Refractive index *n*<sub>*1*</sub> > refractive index *n*<sub>*2*</sub> (air)

blocks.md: ***Diagram showing refraction, the critical angle and total internal reflection***

- Two conditions are necessary for total internal reflection to occur:

  - The light must be going from a** more dense medium** into a **less dense** one
  - The** angle of incidence** must be **greater** than the **critical angle**

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: If asked to name the phenomena make sure you **give the whole name** - Total Internal Reflection. Remember: Total Internal Reflection occurs when going from a **more dense to **a** less dense** material and **ALL** of the light is reflected. If asked to explain what is meant by the **critical angle**, you can draw the diagram above (showing the three semi-circular blocks).
